subject: EdgeVault DPA addendum: redacted subprocessor manifest and export mapping walkthrough
messages:
From: Maria Gomez <maria.gomez@edgevault.com>
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Cc: support@edgevault.com
Date: 2028-05-29T09:22:00-07:00
Subject: Request: redacted subprocessor list + export mapping for DPA addendum

Hi Lauren,

Thanks for the call this morning. Legal at EdgeVault has asked us to provide a redacted subprocessor manifest and a simple export/data-flow mapping to support execution of the DPA addendum. They want a version that we can share with their procurement team without exposing partner account IDs or internal hostnames.

Could you send: 1) a redacted subprocessor roster that shows vendor name, country, processing role, and whether they handle EU data; and 2) a one-page export path diagram or table that lists where data might transit (region level only).

We anticipate a quick turn — procurement would like to review by end of day Thursday. If anything needs a non-disclosure step or an escrow pattern, please flag it.

Attach: sample_manifest_request.txt (we will attach a list of fields).

— Maria Gomez
Head of Procurement, EdgeVault Solutions
From: lauren_bishop@redwood.com
To: Maria Gomez <maria.gomez@edgevault.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.com, neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Date: 2028-05-29T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: redacted subprocessor list + export mapping for DPA addendum

Hi Maria — thanks for the note and the timeline. Looping in Kimberly from Legal and Neha from Privacy Ops to help produce a redacted package that matches procurement needs.

Plan:
- Kimberly to confirm any legal redaction rules for the DPA addendum and whether a separate NDA is required.
- Privacy Ops (Neha) will prepare a redacted manifest (vendor name, country, processing role, EU_data_flag) and a condensed export mapping (region-level transit only).
- I'll send a cover note and the DocuSign link pointing to the draft addendum so procurement can correlate documents.

Do either of you need additional context from EdgeVault (e.g., specific account scopes or target environments)? Maria — if you can confirm whether the procurement reviewer is comfortable with vendor names (versus anonymized labels), that will decide how aggressive we should be with redaction.

Thanks,
Lauren Bishop
Senior Manager, Customer Security
Redwood Inference
From: kimberly_park@redwood.com
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.com, Maria Gomez <maria.gomez@edgevault.com>
Cc: neha_kapoor@redwood.com, andrew.mccabe@finlegal.com
Date: 2028-05-29T12:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: redacted subprocessor list + export mapping for DPA addendum

Hi all,

Quick guidance from Legal: we can provide a redacted manifest that omits internal account IDs, hostnames, and commercial pricing tiers. We should keep vendor legal names and country of operation. If EdgeVault procurement requires fully anonymized labels (Vendor A/B), we will need a short mutual NDA covering 7 days of restricted use — Andrew from FinLegal is cc'd for the NDA template.

Additionally, to make the export mapping DPA-friendly, Privacy Ops should provide region-level transit (e.g., EU -> US, EU -> APAC) and mark whether any subprocessor performs cross-border storage (yes/no).

I'm attaching a redaction guidance template that Privacy Ops can use as a checklist. Once Neha produces the draft, Legal will do a single pass for privileged fields.

Attachments: redaction_guidance_template.docx

— Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Data & Privacy
Redwood Inference
From: neha_kapoor@redwood.com
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.com, kimberly_park@redwood.com, Maria Gomez <maria.gomez@edgevault.com>
Date: 2028-05-29T15:42:00-07:00
Subject: Draft: redacted subprocessor manifest + export mapping (v1)

Hi Maria and team — attached are the first pass files: edgevault_subprocessor_manifest_redacted_v1.xlsx and a one-page PDF export table (embedded in the XLSX as a cover tab).

Summary of redactions performed:
- Removed customer-specific account IDs and internal hostnames.
- Replaced environment-specific suffixes (prod-*) with environment labels (prod/test).
- Kept vendor legal names, country, processing role, and a boolean column EU_Data_Processing.
- Added a note column for 'onshore fallback available' where relevant.

Questions for EdgeVault:
1) Are vendor legal names acceptable to procurement, or do you prefer Vendor 1/2 anonymization?
2) Does procurement need timeline details (retention/backup jurisdictions) or is region-level transit sufficient?

We have included the DocuSign link in the cover note to correlate files with the DPA addendum. Please find the redaction guidance template attached for transparency.

Attachments: edgevault_subprocessor_manifest_redacted_v1.xlsx, dpa_addendum_draft-edgevault.pdf

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
Privacy Operations Lead
Redwood Inference
From: Maria Gomez <maria.gomez@edgevault.com>
To: neha_kapoor@redwood.com, lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Cc: andrew.mccabe@finlegal.com
Date: 2028-05-30T16:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Draft: redacted subprocessor manifest + export mapping (v1)

Neha / Lauren — this is perfect, thank you. Procurement reviewed the sample and confirmed vendor legal names are acceptable; no further anonymization needed. Region-level transit is sufficient for now.

Two quick asks before we close: 1) can you mark vendors that have HSM/KMS access with an asterisk (procurement wants to know key custody posture); 2) add a single line in the cover note indicating the retained copies and retention window for the evidence packet.

We will sign the DPA addendum once we see the final manifest and the DocuSign link. Andrew — let us know if the NDA is required; procurement doesn't think it's necessary at this stage.

— Maria
